description: Bring Your Own Device - Enterprise policy allowing employees to use personal mobile devices for work, requiring containerization and security controls.
Choose Your Own Device - Enterprise policy where employees select a mobile device from a company-approved list, but purchase and own it themselves.
Corporate-Owned, Personally Enabled - Organization owns and manages the mobile device, but allows employees to use it for limited personal tasks.
Mobile Device Management - Security software deployed to remotely provision, monitor, enforce encryption, and wipe corporate mobile hardware.
Mobile Application Management - Software focusing strictly on securing and controlling corporate apps and data on a device without managing the whole OS.
Unified Endpoint Management - Comprehensive platform combining traditional PC management with mobile device management into a single control panel.
Internet of Things - Network of physical smart devices (sensors, appliances) connected to the internet, often lacking strong built-in security features.
Operational Technology - Hardware and software that monitors or controls physical devices, processes, and infrastructure operations in real time.
Industrial Control System - Integrated hardware/software controls used to monitor and operate industrial production lines and critical infrastructure.
Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition - Specialized high-level architecture that monitors and controls large-scale industrial operations across large geographical areas.
Industrial Internet of Things - Connected sensors and instruments integrated into industrial applications to improve operational efficiency and telemetry.
Unmanned Aerial Vehicle - Drones and autonomous aircraft requiring secured wireless command-and-control communication links.
